lesson.subtitle: Lesson 10 -- The Place That Changed Me
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Bruna Viana da Silva Rocha | Lesson 10 -- The Place That Changed Me

listenings.text: I am not going to tell you where it is, because the name does the wrong thing to people. It is a street that is nine blocks long and does not go anywhere. There is a laundromat that has been open since nineteen sixty-two, and a woman who sits outside it, who knows the name of every dog on that street and none of the owners. The building where I lived had a fire escape that everybody used as a balcony, which is illegal, and which nobody has ever stopped. What changed me was not the street. It was that I arrived somewhere nobody was waiting for me, and by the fourth month there was a place where, if I did not show up, somebody would notice. That is the whole thing. That is what a place that changes you actually does. It is not the buildings. It is the first time somebody says your name before you say it.

I went back last spring, twenty-one years later, and I want to be careful, because everybody who does this tells the same lie. They say it had changed. It had not changed much at all. The bakery that I thought I had invented in my head was still there, with the same sign. The square where I used to sit was the same square. What had changed was that I was no longer the person for whom that place was an escape. I stood in the middle of it for about an hour waiting to feel something, and what I felt was that it was a nice square, in a nice town, that had absolutely nothing to do with me anymore. And I want to say this part, because nobody says it. That was not sad. That was the proof that the thing had worked. You do not keep the place. You keep who you became there.
